subject.title: GitHub OAuth consent still shows personal ClawdHub / steipete branding (reopen of #2524)

question: Should production GitHub authentication be moved to a newly created OpenClaw-owned OAuth application or should the existing legacy application be transferred to official ownership?
rationale: Both paths affect production credentials and the authentication trust boundary, and only maintainers with access to the existing OAuth application, official GitHub organization, and Convex production environment can choose and execute the safe rotation path.

options.title: Create and rotate
options.body: Create an officially branded organization-owned OAuth application, rotate production credentials atomically, and retire the personal application after web and CLI validation.

options.title: Transfer the existing app
options.body: Transfer the current OAuth application to official ownership, update its branding and URLs, then verify that its existing credentials and callbacks remain valid.

recommendation.title: Create and rotate
recommendation.body: Create an officially branded organization-owned OAuth application, rotate production credentials atomically, and retire the personal application after web and CLI validation.

likelyOwner.reason: The live consent screen identifies the existing OAuth application with the `steipete` account, making that owner the most likely person needed to transfer or retire it.
